validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all checked. NYMarc was a real, actively-promoted Iroquois Gas Transmission System, L.P. open-season project: a Nov 17, 2009 Iroquois press release announced a non-binding open season (bids due Jan 29, 2010) for a ~66-mile, 36-inch natural gas pipeline interconnecting Tennessee Gas Pipeline (Wantage, Sussex County, NJ) and Millennium Pipeline (Minisink, Orange County, NY) with the Iroquois mainline at Pleasant Valley, NY -- recovered via a working Wayback Machine capture of the PDF at iroquois.com/documents/Iroquois_NYMarcOS_PR.pdf (the sheet's own dead second citation, 'Iroquois Announces NYMarc Open Season', confirmed via url_verifier as a live HTTP 404 at its original iroquois.com URL and never crawled by Wayback under that specific notice_id -- but the underlying press-release PDF itself WAS separately archived and is fully readable). A companion May 13, 2010 Iroquois project brochure (also recovered via Wayback: iroquois.com/project/documents/NYMarcBrochure05-13-10.pdf) gives full specs. Independent third-party corroboration of existence/classification comes from a Penn State Extension 'PA Natural Gas Pipeline Roundup' slide deck (Dave Messersmith, Marcellus Education Team; source cited as FERC; dated ~April 2013), which lists 'NYMarc (Iroquois)' among tracked Marcellus/Utica-era gas pipeline projects. DUPLICATE: checked against the other 44 rows in the batch 5 roster by name/route -- no plausible overlap (NYMarc's Wantage NJ -> Pleasant Valley NY corridor does not match any other roster entry). CLASSIFICATION: correctly an interstate natural gas transmission project (FERC would have been the lead permitting agency per both primary documents). Also checked whether NYMarc might have been built/completed under a different, later Iroquois project name (the finding type flagged for sibling rows P0376/P0380/P2008) -- considered and ruled out both 'South-to-North (SoNo)' (a distinct Dec-2013-open-season Iroquois project on a different Waddington/Canajoharie/Brookfield corridor) and the 'Wright Interconnect/Transfer Compressor' project (a distinct compressor-only project at Wright, NY) and the modern 'Enhancement by Compression (ExC)' project (compression-only uprate, no new pipe, different scope entirely) -- none match NYMarc's specific NJ/Wantage-to-Pleasant-Valley routing or 36-inch new-build scope; no evidence NYMarc was renamed or absorbed into another built project. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: despite the open season and a glossy investment-grade brochure, no evidence was found (SEC EDGAR full-text search for 'NYMarc'/'NY Marc': 0 relevant hits; open web search: no FERC docket number located) that NYMarc ever reached a formal FERC certificate application -- it appears to have stalled at the pre-filing/open-season stage, consistent with an eventual quiet cancellation, but that cancellation itself remains unsourced (see status_reviews and the fills below).

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's ShelvedYear=2010 is in tension with the primary-source timeline: Iroquois's OWN glossy NYMarc investment brochure is dated May 13, 2010 -- four months AFTER the open season closed (Jan 29, 2010) -- and actively promotes the project ('Scheduled in-service date is fall 2014', '$500 million investment'), and the project's FAQ page (iroquois.com/project/nymarc-project-faq.asp) was still live on Iroquois's own website as late as the Dec 26, 2010 Wayback capture. A project actively being marketed with a new brochure and live FAQ page for most/all of 2010 does not fit '2010' as a shelving year. Compounding this, an independent, FERC-sourced Penn State Extension slide deck dated ~April 2013 still lists NYMarc among 'Potential Projects' (not 'Approved or Pending', but also not flagged dead) -- in tension with the sheet's CancelledYear=2012. I could NOT find any source stating a corrected shelved or cancelled year (the trail goes cold after the April 2013 slide -- 13+ years of total silence: no further Iroquois press release, no FERC docket, no SEC filing, no trade-press mention located despite an extensive search), so I am NOT proposing a replacement value -- flagging the contradiction for a human researcher to weigh rather than guessing at a specific year.

fills.researcher_notes: No source explicitly states NYMarc was cancelled/withdrawn/abandoned. Searched exhaustively: (1) the sheet's own two wiki citations -- citation 1 is the BANNED abarrelfull.wikidot.com (never cited, read for leads only per standing rule); citation 2 (iroquois.com/formnoticedetail.asp?Notice_id_out=2000, 'Iroquois Announces NYMarc Open Season') returns a live HTTP 404 (confirmed via url_verifier) and was NEVER crawled by the Wayback Machine under that specific notice_id (confirmed via a full CDX scan of iroquois.com/formnoticedetail.asp* -- 125 captures found, all for notice_id_out 3334-3922, none anywhere near 2000 -- this is a genuine archival gap, not a rate-limit artifact, since the CDX API itself returned successfully). (2) SEC EDGAR full-text search for 'NYMarc' and 'NY Marc' -- 0 relevant hits. (3) Open web search for a FERC docket number, cancellation notice, or withdrawal announcement -- none found; NYMarc appears to have never reached a formal FERC certificate filing at all. (4) The only independently-dated post-2010 record found, a Penn State Extension/FERC-sourced slide deck (~April 2013), lists NYMarc as still 'Potential' rather than cancelled. Given 13+ years of total subsequent silence (no docket, no filing, no press, no further Iroquois materials) and no trace of the pipeline ever being built, 'cancelled' as the general category is plausible and uncontradicted by anything found -- but it remains an inference, not a sourced fact. See status_reviews for the fuller status assessment.

The last independently-dated public trace of the project is an April-2013 Penn State Extension/FERC-sourced slide still listing it as 'Potential' (not yet dead, but not advancing either). Given 13+ years of complete subsequent silence -- no FERC filing, no further Iroquois materials, no SEC disclosure, no trade press -- 'cancelled' is a reasonable and uncontradicted characterization of the project's current state, so I am CONFIRMING the Status value rather than proposing a change. However, I found evidence that undercuts the SPECIFIC dates: Iroquois was still actively promoting NYMarc via a new brochure and a live FAQ page well into (and past) 2010, which is in tension with the sheet's ShelvedYear=2010, and the April-2013 'Potential' listing is in tension with CancelledYear=2012 -- see the two 'spec' concerns flagged in validity[] and the corresponding UNRESOLVED Shelved/Cancelled fills. Because no source gives a corrected date for either, ShelvedCancelledType stays 'inferred' (no change to 'confirmed' proposed) -- a directionally-plausible but genuinely undated, unsourced cancellation is exactly what 'inferred' is for.
